full_judgment: 11. Moreover, in this suit the factum of possession is a very material thing and the learned trial Court held that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land, but the learned appellate Court held that the plaintiff could prove his possession in the suit land. Admittedly by the said 4 deeds 24 decimals of land have been transferred by 4 brothers including the plaintiff and out of this 24 decimals plaintiff's claim is for 6 decimals. In the schedule of the plaint the plaintiff has shown this 6 decimals in plot No.351 out of 13 plots. There is no case by the plaintiff that by amicable portion among the brothers the plaintiff got said 6 decimals of land and he is in possession of that 6 decimals of land. The plaintiff in his examination in-chief stated that he is in possession of the suit land. To the query of the Court, plaintiff stated that there is a `doba' in suit plot No. 351 and that the plaintiff along with his other brothers are the owners of that ditch and the defendants do not use the said ditch and that the defendants land is to the eastern side of that ditch. In cross-examination he could not say how much land he got from his father and he could not say how much land he sold out. He also could not tell how much nal land he got. He denied the suggestion that at the instance of his brothers he filed the present suit. He further stated that he paid tax including municipal tax for the suit land, but he had not pay tax for the present year. He stated that he cannot produce the rent receipt for the suit land. He stated that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made a wall in the north southern direction in the suit land for their share. He also stated that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made a wall in the southern side of plot no. 351. P.W.2 who is the husband of the sister of the plaintiff in his cross-examination stated that he cannot tell how much land the plaintiff possesses in the suit dag. He stated that the defendant Nos.1- 4 have a house in the northern bank of the ditch and that they are in possession by placing a fence. He stated that he does not know how much land of the disputed deed the plaintiff possesses. P.W.3 Monindra Chandra Roy stated in his examination in-chief that the plaintiff possesses the suit land, but in cross-examination he stated that he does not know the dag and khatian number of the suit land. The defendant examined 2 D.Ws including the defendant No. 3. It appears, regarding possession of the defendants they corroborated each other and no material contradiction came out from their cross-examination.
